VRChat is not responsible for maintaining SDK packages made by the community. The officially recommended way to test an in-progress avatar is to build and test it in the client.

In an SDK project containing no community packages, your repro steps display the values changing in the contact receiver even while no animator is assigned. These are passed on to the animator controller once one has been assigned to the avatar's animator.

If you have a repro case for the proximity parameter and advanced parameters behaving differently in a project with no community packages in it, please feel free to report this to us.

details:
**Summary**

In SDK 3.10.6, Advanced Contact Parameters (e.g. Sender Local Position) don't update in Gesture Manager or Av3 Emulator play mode unless the avatar root's Animator has a Controller assigned. Nothing is logged when this fails. Build & Test in the client works correctly, so this only affects the editor workflow.

**Reproduction**

1. Avatar with a contact receiver using Advanced Parameters (e.g. Sender Local Position X/Y/Z), with those parameters in the FX controller.

2. Leave the avatar root Animator's Controller field empty.

3. Enter play mode in Gesture Manager. The parameters stay at 0.

4. Assign a controller containing those parameter names to the Animator's Controller field. They now update. (A dummy controller with just the parameter names is enough.)

Av3 Emulator doesn't update them in either case.

**What I found in the SDK source**

- `AvatarDynamicsSetup.cs` creates an `AnimParameterAccessAvatarSDK` per enabled advanced parameter, bound to the avatar root Animator.

- Its constructor looks the name up in `animator.parameters`. With no controller, nothing is found and the accessor marks itself invalid. Every later write is then a silent no-op.

- Emulators that supply their own accessor for the base contact parameter have no documented way to do the same for the advanced ones, so those fall back to the SDK's root-Animator version.

**Requests**

1. Log a console warning when an advanced-parameter accessor is created invalid (Animator missing or no controller, or the parameter not found).

2. Don't depend on the root Animator's controller for this. Resolve the parameters from the descriptor's FX controller instead, or create the accessors lazily.

3. Document how emulator authors should supply accessors for the advanced parameters, since the feature shipped with both major emulators not yet handling it.

SDK 3.10.6, Unity 2022.3.22f1, Gesture Manager 3.9.9. Related report on the Gesture Manager tracker: https://github.com/BlackStartx/VRC-Gesture-Manager/issues/105
title: Advanced Contact Parameters silently fail in emulators (E.G Gesture Manager) unless the avatar root Animator has a controller
